subject: POC trial: model selection, success criteria & kickoff
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@brightshop.io>, Jake Park <jake.park@brightshop.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: POC trial: model selection, success criteria & kickoff

Hi Lena / Jake —

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about BrightShop's checkout assistant use case and multilingual traffic. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the POC plan: 

1) Recap of goals / success criteria
- Primary goal: reduce automated escalation to live agent by >=30% on post-checkout queries (order status, returns, coupons) during the trial.
- Quality threshold: intent accuracy >= 88% and precision/recall on entity extraction within 5 points of your current baseline for EN (we'll validate with a 200-sample human check).
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for 512-token contexts in the hosted EU/US region (we'll run a perf benchmark).
- Cost guidance: target conversational token cost <= $0.004/token on average across the POC traffic profile.

2) Proposed model selection for trial
- Primary model (quality-first): meta/llama-2-13b-chat (FP16 or int8 quantized variant) — good balance of instruction-following and latency when served on dedicated GPUs.
- Fallback model (throughput/cost): meta/llama-2-7b-chat (quantized q4 variants) — used for low-latency, high-concurrency routes.
- Multilingual note: for DE/FR traffic we can test the same Llama-2 variants and add a small XLM-based ensemble if we see systematic quality drops. We'll include a separate 200-sample test per language for manual review.

3) Evaluation plan
- Automated eval: intent accuracy and entity extraction automated tests over a 1k synthetic+prod-like sample.
- Human eval: 200 random samples per language (EN/DE/FR) for subjective quality and edge-case coverage.
- Performance: run perf sweep for p50/p95/p99 on 128/512/1024 context lengths.

4) Ownership & timeline
- Redwood AE / PM: Marissa Cole (manages logistics and success criteria)
- Redwood SE/tech lead: Aditya Rao (model selection, perf tuning)
- Redwood infra engineer: Dev Patel (integration & logs)
- Customer POC lead: Lena Hoffman

Proposed timeline:
- Tech kickoff: week of 2026-04-19 (30–60 min).
- PoC setup & perf baseline: 1 week.
- Trial run & evaluation: 2 weeks.
- Final review & next steps: week of 2026-05-10.

Attachments: Redwood-POC-plan.pdf (high-level plan + eval checklist).

Next steps: Lena — confirm kickoff availability (we'll propose 4/19 or 4/20), confirm attendees, and any additional compliance/residency constraints. Aditya / Dev — I copied you for model perf notes and quantization recommendations.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection, success criteria & kickoff

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying questions before we lock the kickoff: 

1) Multilingual quality: do you have prior benchmarks for German (DE) performance on Llama-2 variants? We need to make sure not to regress on DE channel.
2) Fallback model: if we use the 7b quantized fallback, do you expect a significant drop in entity extraction quality? We can accept some drop for generic chit-chat but not for order numbers/return codes.
3) Data residency / compliance: we prefer EU-hosted inference for EU traffic. Is the hosted API EU region SLA-able for the trial, or do we need a dedicated/reserved instance?

If you can confirm those, I can confirm attendees for the kickoff — I'll include our engineering lead (Jake Park) and Natalia from Ops if needed.

Lena
BrightShop
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@brightshop.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-13T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection, success criteria & kickoff

Hi Lena — quick technical answers to your questions: 

1) German benchmarks: we have internal evals showing Llama-2-13b-chat performs within ~3–5 points of EN on intent/classification for commerce queries when prompts are localized. We will run a focused 200-sample manual eval for DE and FR during the POC to validate. If we see larger gaps, we can try an XLM-based model or a small translation+prompting pipeline.

2) 7b fallback quality: quantized 7b models generally have a measurable drop in extraction precision (~4–8 points) depending on the entity type. For structured fields like order numbers/return codes we can keep a small rule-based extractor (regex + verification) as a safety net in the pipeline while using 7b for conversational routing to reduce latency/cost. That avoids incorrect entity substitutions.

3) Residency: Redwood hosted API supports region-scoped endpoints (us / eu / apac). For the trial we can provision the EU-hosted endpoint with normal hosted credentials (no extra infra charge) and run the EU traffic through it. If you require contract-level data residency guarantees or an isolated VPC, that's typically a Dedicated/Private engagement (we can discuss).

Technical notes / recommendations:
- Start with meta/llama-2-13b-chat (FP16) for the quality route. Use q4_0 quantized 13b for perf sweep; fallback to llama-2-7b-chat-q4 for low-latency routes.
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeated session prompts to keep p95 low.
- We'll provide a small evaluation harness (script + sample set) that you can run on your side and share results via Drive.

Happy to walk through the perf profile at kickoff.

- Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
